title: Does an Edge Make the Figure?
selectionMethod: Internal 1-5 judgments in order: originality, visual necessity, interaction meaning, feasibility. Reasons, not totals, determine the choice. Scores are planning notes, never displayed as evidence or outcomes.

hypotheses.idea: Hold color and area constant while comparing an edge-attached strip with an enclosed square
hypotheses.reason: Selected: the two simultaneous fields make equal quantity auditable while changing the boundary relation directly, extending Day022 without repeating its single sliding split.

hypotheses.idea: Rotate one equal-area split from vertical to horizontal
hypotheses.reason: A clean orientation check, but both regions would still touch the frame and the question would be more about reading direction and gravity than containment.

hypotheses.idea: Compare a centered square with an off-center square at the same size
hypotheses.reason: Position would be isolated more narrowly, yet it would not answer the unresolved question about whether touching the frame changes figure-ground assignment.

hypotheses.idea: Let a colored disk cross the frame edge while preserving its visible area
hypotheses.reason: Visually strong, but preserving visible area while clipping requires changing the disk size and introduces curvature, clipping and implied continuation together.

hypotheses.idea: Compare one closed contour with four separated corner marks
hypotheses.reason: Closure becomes explicit, but it returns to Day012's contour-completion territory and would compare line drawings rather than occupied color fields.

hypotheses.idea: Place the same word inside and across a color boundary
hypotheses.reason: Editorially concrete, but typography, legibility and semantic grouping would compete with the more basic figure-ground question.

hypotheses.idea: Compare equal-area convex and concave regions
hypotheses.reason: Relevant to Gestalt research, but perimeter and local edge density would vary substantially and responsive exact-area authoring would need more complex paths.

hypotheses.idea: Reveal equal color area as one block or many distributed dots
hypotheses.reason: It would make grouping visible, but spatial frequency and numerosity would dominate and repeat Day015's screen-pattern vocabulary.

hypotheses.idea: Animate an enclosed region until it touches the frame
hypotheses.reason: The transition could dramatize attachment, but timing, motion and change history would become extra variables and reduced-motion support would require a second form.

hypotheses.idea: Ask visitors to draw the boundary they think belongs to the figure
hypotheses.reason: It could surface individual constructions, but saved drawings would require a research protocol, privacy decisions and interpretation that are outside this implementation-only day.

variable: The highlighted region's boundary construction: a full-height strip attached to a frame edge versus a centered enclosed square.
comparison: Both square fields use the same two opaque sRGB colors and the highlighted region occupies the same 16-64% area. The strip width equals the selected share; the enclosed square side is the square root of that share.
constants: Equal square field dimensions within the same viewport
Same highlighted-area percentage in both constructions
Same two CSS color values and full opacity
No texture, animation, score, stored response or participant-data collection
challenge: If judgments do not cluster, reverse with color assignment or strip side, or are better explained by compactness, perimeter, position, luminance or terminology, do not attribute a general figure-ground effect to closure or edge contact alone.
researchLedForm: Two large square fields appear side by side before the controls. One region touches three frame edges; the other is surrounded on four sides. A shared area control, strip-side move and color swap expose dependencies without assigning a correct figure.
mediaDecision: Live HTML and CSS are necessary because one control must preserve mathematically equal area across two responsive constructions and remain reversible by keyboard and touch. A raster image freezes one state; video adds time; generated imagery cannot guarantee exact geometry and would introduce texture or lighting. No external image is used.

revisits.question: Counterbalance construction order, strip side, color assignment and starting share; collect separate figure, background, dominance and confidence judgments.
Compare equal-perimeter and equal-compactness variants, calibrated versus ordinary displays, and current web geometry support without treating one cue as isolated.
